newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN POST OFFICE GETS FIVE YEARS TO SHAPE UP.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN POST OFFICE GETS FIVE YEARS TO SHAPE UP.

text.p: South Africa's ailing Post Office has been given five years to eradicate losses and provide a more efficient service, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo said on Tuesday.

He told the parliamentary finance committee that it had also been decided that the Post Office -- which is off-budget because it is supposed to be self-funding -- would be brought into the normal budgetary process.
Legislation to this effect would be presented to parliament this year.
The Post Office would be given a maximum of five more years during which it would be subsidised by government while adopting clear strategies to become self-sufficient.

These strategies would include tariff increases, but also steps to make the Post Office more efficient and provide a wider range of services such as the payment of pensions, housing subsidies and rural financing.

Naidoo repeatedly said that there could be no "quick fix" to the Post Office's problems. Several committee members said, however, that they believed a five year plan would not be enough and some form of radical intervention was called for.
The committee had on Monday attacked the apparent inability of the Post Office to curb losses and asked Naidoo to give it a special briefing on the situation as soon as possible.
In 1996/97 it should have posted a surplus of 10.6 million rand, but instead has a defecit of 572 million rand.
The Post Office should also start providing services to previously neglected black areas while closing down some services in areas that were over-serviced.
Experts from other countries had been consulted on how best to make the Post Office profitable and there had been a freeze on new appointments.
